subtopic: Nutrition and mood in general terms
passage:
In Room 214 of the boys' hostel, Sumit's dinner was the same every night: instant noodles at midnight, a packet of chips and a fizzy drink. He skipped the mess because the queue was long, and he usually slept through breakfast. By the end of the month he felt tired all the time, dragged himself to lectures and couldn't be bothered to call home.
One afternoon Nirmala aunty, who ran the mess counter, caught him buying chips. "You look like a wilted spinach leaf," she said. "Come at one tomorrow. I'll keep dal and curd for you."
He went. Then he started taking a banana from the counter on his way out. Some nights it was still noodles, but now he added an egg. After a couple of weeks he noticed he wasn't nodding off in afternoon labs.

qa.q: What did Sumit eat every night at midnight?
qa.a: Instant noodles, with a packet of chips and a fizzy drink.

qa.q: How was Sumit feeling by the end of the month?
qa.a: Sumit felt tired and unmotivated, dragging himself to lectures and not bothering to call home.

qa.q: What small upgrades did Sumit make?
qa.a: Eating dal and curd at the mess, taking a banana on the way out, and adding an egg to the noodles.

qa.q: How might Nirmala aunty see Sumit?
qa.a: Nirmala aunty seems to see a worn-out student who needs looking after, teasing him kindly and keeping food aside.

grounding: A young adult living on late-night instant food feels tired and low, and small upgrades like dal, curd, fruit and eggs help without a perfect diet.

subtopic: Nutrition and mood in general terms
passage:
Hi Ritu Didi,
You asked why I sound so flat on calls. Honestly, I think it's the food. At the PG in Hyderabad, dinner is whatever the delivery app has at 11 pm, usually fried stuff or instant noodles. Lunch is a samosa from the canteen. I've been sleepy in class and grumpy for no reason, and I skipped cricket twice because I just felt heavy.
I remembered what you said about small changes, not a perfect diet. So I've started buying curd and bananas from the shop downstairs, and I asked Mrs Reddy on the ground floor if I could pay for her home-cooked dal-rice three nights a week. She said yes!
It's only been ten days, but I'm less foggy in the mornings. I even went back to cricket.
Love,
Tejas

qa.q: What does Tejas buy from the shop downstairs?
How has Tejas been feeling at the PG?
qa.a: Tejas has felt flat, sleepy and grumpy, heavy enough to skip cricket twice.
It adds small, affordable upgrades like curd, bananas and home-cooked dal-rice on some nights, rather than demanding a perfect diet.

qa.q: How might Ritu Didi feel reading the email?
qa.a: Ritu Didi would likely feel relieved that Tejas remembered the advice and is feeling less foggy.

grounding: A young adult on late-night fried and instant food feels tired and low, and small upgrades lift energy without a perfect diet.
